(d) No host group needed, so nothing has to be secured in advance. RAISED FROM 3 TO 4 THIS PASS because the open condition that held it at 3 has been resolved as far as public sources allow: DMM's own scope statement is approach-agnostic, 'aims to advance novel insight into the mechanism, diagnosis and therapy of human disease' and 'covers a diverse range of diseases and model systems', with no restriction to animal or cellular models, and the grant text asks that the MEETING fall in areas covered by the journal, not that her own paper be publishable there. Name: ESRS Short-Term Research Fellowship
Geography_Eligible: Visit must be to a laboratory in the ESRS Network of Sleep Research Laboratories, i.e. a European host institution different from the applicant's own. No nationality restriction found.
Host_Requirement: MANDATORY AND PRIOR: literal condition is that the applicant must 'have an agreement with a host laboratory in the ESRS Network of Sleep Research Laboratories'. The host must be secured before applying and must be a member lab of that network, which is a closed list, not any sleep lab.
Amount_EUR: up to 2800 for a three-month fellowship
Years_PostPhD_Window: No post-PhD window found. The only career-stage language is a preference, not a cut-off: 'Particular preference is given to candidates in the early stages of their careers'. No requirement that the PhD be already awarded was found, so unlike most of her options this one may be usable before her February 2028 defence.
Eligibility_Key_Conditions: ESRS membership is required ('Applicants must be ESRS members'); a prior agreement with a host laboratory inside the ESRS Network of Sleep Research Laboratories; the visit must be central to basic, translational or clinical sleep research and NOT purely clinical or educational training; preference for early-career candidates; an output is expected, preferably a full paper including a preprint, or at minimum an abstract accepted at an international meeting, and the output may come after the fellow returns home. Deadline not confirmed: the only date available is an aggregator forecast of March 2027, explicitly labelled 'Anticipated' and the entry itself flagged 'Forecasted'.
Fit_Rationale: Plausible but conditional, and the condition is money, not profile. The mechanism matches her proven way of working better than anything else in the sleep block: a three-month collaborative visit to another lab is exactly the shape of her QIMR Berghofer and Japan stays, and it serves research line 3 (genetics of sleep in infants and toddlers) with a sleep-genetics host. It is also the only sleep-side instrument found so far with no evidence of a 'PhD already awarded' requirement, so in principle it is reachable from mid-2027 (end of residency, 22-05-2027) rather than only after February 2028. What stops it being a 4 is the size: up to 2800 EUR for three months is a travel and subsistence top-up, not a salary, so it only works bolted onto an existing contract or another fellowship, and it cannot fund a stay on its own. Three conditions to resolve before it is actionable: ESRS membership (no minimum seniority of membership found, so it can be joined at any time, unlike the SES one-year rule), a host lab that is actually inside the ESRS Network of Sleep Research Laboratories, and a salary source for the three months. Effort is low once the host says yes.
Competition_Basis: No number of fellowships awarded per cycle, no applicant counts and no success rate were found; the ESRS site could not be read to check, so no estimate is made rather than a guessed one.
Next_Action: Two things, in this order. 1) Join the ESRS (SUB proposal this pass): membership gates all four ESRS grant lines and has no seniority requirement, so it is cheap to fix now. 2) needs host: see L-#### candidates, but filtered specifically against the ESRS Network of Sleep Research Laboratories member list, because a host outside that network does not qualify. Name: ASHG Trainee Research Excellence Award (formerly Charles J. Epstein Trainee Research Awards)
Geography_Eligible: No nationality restriction stated; trainees worldwide compete through the Annual Meeting abstract system. Travel to the USA would need a visa or ESTA, which is a logistics note, not an eligibility bar. ASHG 2027 is in Nashville (see SRC-0110).
Host_Requirement: None. No host lab needed; the only third party is a nominator/mentor whose name and e-mail go on the abstract form.
Amount_EUR: Reported as USD 750 plus complimentary Annual Meeting registration for the roughly 60 semifinalists, and a further USD 250 for the 18 finalists (about 650-1550 EUR equivalent). Figures come from a secondary summary of the official page, which is behind a member login, so they are not Tier 1 confirmed.
Duration: One-off, tied to the ASHG Annual Meeting (ASHG 2027, Nashville).
Years_PostPhD_Window: No post-PhD window: predoctoral and postdoctoral trainees, reportedly up to six years of postdoctoral training. She would apply as a predoctoral trainee, so the clock is not binding before her February 2028 defence.
Eligibility_Key_Conditions: Reportedly: ASHG member; predoctoral or postdoctoral trainee (genetic counselling trainees included), not more than six years in postdoctoral training; first author on an abstract submitted to the ASHG Annual Meeting; name and e-mail of a nominator or mentor, who need not be an ASHG member. There is no separate application form: the option to be considered is a checkbox inside the Annual Meeting abstract submission form, which opens in spring. About 60 semifinalists and 18 finalists, notified in late summer. All of this is from a secondary summary because the official award page gates its own content behind a member login.
Fit_Rationale: (a) ASHG is the natural home congress for her first research line, statistical genetics of complex traits, and for the second, GWAS and PRS of psychiatric disorders: an abstract on the QIMR empirical work opens exactly the line she wants to continue. (b) Eligibility against her clocks: she is a predoctoral trainee until February 2028, so both the trainee definition and the six-year postdoctoral limit are satisfied with room to spare for the 2027 and 2028 editions; the condition she does not yet meet is ASHG membership, which is a payment, not a career clock. First authorship is satisfiable: both manuscripts under review are hers as first author. (c) The application is a checkbox and an abstract, not a dossier: no research plan, no budget, no host letter, so the real work is writing one abstract she would write anyway plus asking her supervisor to be named nominator. (d) No host group needed, which is what makes this cheap compared with every short-stay scheme in this branch.
Competition_Basis: Merit ranking of trainee-authored abstracts at a meeting that receives thousands of them, with roughly 60 semifinalists and 18 finalists, so the per-abstract odds are not high. What keeps it worth doing is that the marginal cost is almost zero: the abstract is submitted anyway and there is no separate dossier.
Next_Action: Two things, in order: 1) confirm the bases in Tier 1, which needs either an ASHG member login or the ASHG 2027 call for abstracts once it is published (the award page ashg.org/?p=5180 answers 'You must be a member to access this page'); 2) decide on ASHG membership before the spring 2027 abstract window, since membership is a stated requirement and the award rides on the abstract form. Re-check in March 2027.
